Ryan —

Thanks for the clear asks. We've put together a short sanity spreadsheet and the token profile from the trial run (attached). High level answers below; the sheet has the math so you can adjust traffic and prompt lengths.

1) baseline tokens / $ (hosted plan, current public pricing bands):
   - conservative: 0.0015 USD per token-equivalent (assumes standard FP16 model, no quantization, small shared throughput discounts)
   - baseline: 0.0011 USD / token (expected for reserved capacity + modest batching)
   - aggressive: 0.0008 USD / token (dedicated + int8 quant + steady-state batching + prefix cache hit ~35%)
   Note: our "token" in the sheet maps to GPT-style tokens; we included prompt/response breakdown.

2) caching / prefix & KV effects:
   - prefix caching reduces per-request generation tokens by avoiding re-generation for repeated system/prompt prefixes. In the pilot traffic sample we saw 18-42% reduction in generated tokens depending on prompt reuse.
   - KV cache (session state) reduces inner-loop generation for multi-turn flows; TTL and shard locality drive hit-rate. We recommend modeling a low/med/high hit rate: 10% / 30% / 50%.

3) batching assumptions (for p99 latency gating):
   - conservative (p99 target 500ms): per-GPU batch size ~2-4, lower concurrency — plan for fewer generated tokens per-second and higher cost per token.
   - baseline (p99 target 300ms): batch size ~6-12 with dynamic batching; typical throughput improvements 1.6-2.2x over conservative.
   - optimistic (p99 target 200ms): batch size ~12-24 with aggressive packing and prefetch; throughput 2.5-4x but tail latency variance increases.

Actionable: attached AEGIS_MAP_Econ_Sanity.xlsx shows a two-scenario model (baseline + conservative) and a token-profile CSV from the test harness. We've made the assumptions explicit (see sheet tabs: "Assumptions", "Traffic Model", "Calc").

Next steps I propose:

- We (Redwood) finalize MAP dates and deliverables by EOD 11/30 so your procurement can start on 12/1.

Looping Karthik and Ben for any deeper batching/cache clarifications below.

Best —

Evelyn / team / Ryan —

Adding a few technical clarifications to make the MAP gating explicit (copy/paste friendly for the spreadsheet):

- Batching model: Redwood uses continuous/dynamic batching. Effective batch size depends on concurrent inflight requests and request length distribution. For your traffic (median request 400 tokens generated, 800 tokens prompt), assume: concurrency 40 -> effective batch ~8; concurrency 100 -> effective batch ~18. We've added a helper table in the "Assumptions" tab mapping concurrency to batch factor.

- Latency impact: batching improves token-efficiency but increases queueing time. For p99 at 300ms we expect <10% of requests to queue beyond 30ms at batch sizes <=12 for your profile. We included a latency/cost tradeoff slider in the sheet.

- Prefix caching: implementation detail — we cache prefix KV on-host and maintain a small LRU per model shard. Hit rates depend on prompt template stability. For pilot, if you enforce templated prompts for clinical summarization, expect 30%+ hit rate; exploratory free-text flows will be much lower.

- Quantization: switching to int8 reduces GPU memory and can decrease per-token runtime by ~15-35% depending on operator coverage. We flagged in the sheet which model families have safe int8 paths.

- Rate-limiting & throttling fallback: recommend a fallback policy in MAP: if latency SLO breaches, route to smaller (cheaper) model variant or enable partial-response streaming. We've added a sample fallback policy text in sheet.

If you want, Ben and I can run a short 2-hour smoke test with your sample traffic to generate an updated token-profile with caching enabled; that will reduce uncertainty in the model.

-Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
